analysis.title: The great AI rotation (European Equity Strategy)
key_insights: Since early October markets are less willing to fund the AI infrastructure build-out. Firmus withdrew its IPO, CoreWeave 2032 unsecured bond yields touched 15% and its shares fell about 15% the next day, and Elice fell more than 30% below its IPO price on debut before recovering.
The MSCI Europe AI Capex Select index is down about 15% from its early October high, reversing all gains since the late-July low.
The 12-month rolling correlation between the AI Capex Select index and European cyclicals (ex-financials and resources) versus defensives has risen above 90%, from about 25% a year ago.

European cyclicals have underperformed defensives by 11% since the start of October, the worst period since the March 2020 Covid shock (-18%). Semis lag by 15%, mining by 9% and cap goods by 7%. The 'anti-AI' sectors food & beverages (+9%) and personal & household goods (+7%) outperformed.

BofA stays concerned about the AI capex outlook. Rising funding costs squeeze incremental returns, and past capex cycles saw competition erode pricing power and monetisation disappoint. Ramp AI data show US business AI spending flat-lined in recent months as rising token volumes were offset by falling token prices, contrary to Jevons paradox.
A Fed hike this month is a potential amplifier. BofA economists hold a non-consensus call for a 25bp hike while the market prices only about 10%.

The Stoxx 600 is up about 1% since the rotation began. The equity risk premium rose 25bps to 4.6%, a nearly four-month high, from a 24-year low of 4.2% in late September. US HY spreads have widened nearly 70bps from the late-August 19-year low. A lower real yield and higher 12-month forward EPS more than offset the ERP drag.
BofA economists estimate AI capex added nearly 0.7ppts to US GDP growth in H1, implying a drag of about 0.7ppts if capex flatlines and more if it declines.

BofA stays negative on European equities. Its macro projections imply nearly 10% further downside for the Stoxx 600 by Q2 next year (to 580), 5% by year-end (to 610), after a 4% pullback from the early-August record high.

Positioning: underweight semis, capital goods, mining, banks, financial services, insurance, Spain and Italy, and cyclicals versus defensives. Overweight food & beverages, pharma, utilities, telecoms, real estate, consumer durables (luxury), quality, small versus large caps, Switzerland, Germany, UK and France. Marketweight airlines, autos, construction materials, software, energy and chemicals. Underweight value versus growth.

France was raised to overweight after more than 20% underperformance since 2024. The OAT-Bund spread is 170bps, the highest since 2011, and France's forward P/E discount to Europe is 8%, the largest since 2016. The ERP widening in France has been muted relative to the spread.

US-Iran: Strait of Hormuz tanker transits are back to effectively zero after a pick-up following the MoU. Prediction markets give 8% odds of normalisation by January. US gasoline is about $5.1/gal, up close to 20% since early July. The US SPR is the lowest since 1982.
BofA is marketweight energy despite macro-implied downside of more than 20% in relative price, because of US/Iran tensions. Energy has outperformed by 25%+ since early July.

AI fragility indicators: US hyperscaler ROIC fell from 21% to 15.5%, hyperscaler IG spreads and CDS have risen, Oracle 5-year CDS is above 2008 levels, and hyperscaler depreciation is set to exceed $600bn a year. Hyperscalers have underperformed the market by nearly 20% over the past year.

Consensus 12-month forward US hyperscaler capex rose from under $300bn in early 2025 to $1tn. The AI buildout is about 3% of US GDP, above past investment booms. Tech is expected to supply over a quarter of global profits, an all-time high.
Global composite PMI is at an eight-year high (ex-Covid) of 54.2. BofA expects it to fade, with global macro surprises turning negative, US HY spreads widening and the ERP rising.

US growth is strong: final private demand hit a three-year high in Q2 with the Atlanta Fed pointing to more in Q3. The fiscal impulse is likely peaking, with the deficit at 7.4% of GDP versus a projected 6.1% in FY2027. Core inflation is expected near 3% for the rest of 2026.

Markets price 80bps of further Fed hikes over the next year on top of the September hike, versus 70bps of cuts priced at the start of the Iran war. BofA expects real yields and bond yields to fall as growth weakens.

BofA's Stoxx 600 base case sees the 12-month forward P/E de-rating from 13.8x to 13.5x and EPS growth of 9% in 2026 and 4% in 2027, both below consensus. Forward EPS is seen 7% below current all-time highs.
Rule of thumb from BofA's model: every 3pt fall in euro area PMI lowers the Stoxx 600 fair value by about 5%, and every 100bp rise in real yield lowers it by about 5%.

risk_factors: A Fed hike in October could amplify AI funding stress.
AI capex flatlining or declining would drag on US GDP growth and US equities.
Wider French spreads ahead of next year's presidential election.
A sharp spike in credit spreads would offset the benefit of lower bond yields for real estate.
Oil price spikes of the recent magnitude have historically coincided with recession onsets, and the Hormuz standoff keeps oil risk elevated.
Hyperscaler depreciation charges rising above $600bn a year and falling ROIC.
The USD strengthening points to a risk of lost momentum in US manufacturing.
vol_and_positioning: The US MOVE bond volatility index has spiked, typically associated with wider US HY spreads.
The CCC-and-lower HY spread has begun to widen significantly while overall HY spreads remain low.
European cross-sector dispersion is close to a level seen only three times since the financial crisis.
European momentum long-short had record outperformance this year before a pullback since mid-June.
Hyperscaler CDS spreads have risen. Oracle's 5-year CDS is well above its 2008 level, and CoreWeave's 2032 unsecured bonds yielded about 15%.
geopolitical: US-Iran war and the US-Iran Memorandum of Understanding: Strait of Hormuz tanker transits have fallen back to effectively zero after a pick-up following the signing.
Kalshi puts the probability of Hormuz traffic normalising by January at 8%.
French presidential election next year and political noise are widening French bond spreads.
Chinese crude imports fell to a ten-year low of 7.2 mb/d in June and recovered to 9.1 mb/d.

tension_points.bull_case: Consensus expects the global profit boom to last. AI capex adds growth, and the Stoxx 600 is up slightly as lower real yields and higher EPS offset the ERP rise.
tension_points.bear_case: Falling token prices and competition erode pricing power. Funding costs are rising, ROIC has fallen to 15.5%, and neocloud IPOs and bonds are under strain.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence that AI spending resumes rising despite lower token prices, easing the monetisation concern.

tension_points.bull_case: Falling real yields and rising 12-month forward EPS have more than offset the ERP increase, and Europe is at a narrow valuation discount to the US.
tension_points.bear_case: Rising ERP, weaker PMI and EPS downside imply nearly 10% Stoxx 600 downside by Q2 next year.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Global macro surprises staying positive and HY spreads not widening.
